描述_ZN: The Stallion scroll, modern, painted by Xu Beihong, on paper with color, 109.3 cm in length and 53 cm in width.　　Self-titled: "Thirty-seven years of Beihong." Inscription: "Painting of Beihong" in vermilion. Inscribed in the lower right corner with a square seal in vermilion, "Knowing in difficulty".　　Thirty-seven years refers to the thirty-seventh year of the Republic of China (1948), when Xu Beihong was 53 years old.　　The picture depicts a horse on a flat slope in the wilderness, looking back as it tries to move and stop.　　Xu Beihong painted thousands of European horses in the 1920s during his travels to Europe, and at the end of the 1930s, when he went to India to lecture at the International University, he traveled to Kashmir in the western part of the Tibetan Plateau and Darjeeling in the foothills of the Himalayas, and was deeply moved by the tall and tough wild horses on the plateau. Since then, the horses under Xu Beihong's brush not only have beautiful physique, but also have brave vigor and tough endurance. They are long and lean, not as fat as the horses painted by ancient Chinese masters such as Cao Ba, Chen Ma, Han Gan, Zhang Xuan and Zhao Mengfu, but no less majestic. Their nostrils are wide open, indicating that they have great lung capacity and are good at running for a long time. Their long, slender legs and wide hooves suggest their robustness and swiftness when running.
